vulnerability: Unauthorized fake deposits and token drain via self-approval
reason: The public function depositFromOtherContract has no access control and forwards attacker-controlled _depositAmount, _periodId, _isUnlocked, and _from into _autoDeposit. _autoDeposit never transfers tokens from the caller or _from; it only calls token.approve(address(this), _depositAmount), which creates a self-allowance for the pool contract. It then credits user.totalDepositTokens, totalGymnetLocked, and possibly totalGymnetUnlocked, and stores a deposit for _from. An attacker can call depositFromOtherContract with _from = attacker and _isUnlocked = true, setting a large self-allowance and receiving a fake deposit balance without paying any tokens. After the short unlocked delay, the attacker calls withdraw. _withdraw executes token.safeTransferFrom(address(this), msg.sender, depositDetails.depositTokens), which uses the self-allowance established in _autoDeposit to transfer real pool tokens to the attacker. This drains the contract balance and can be repeated to steal all tokens held by the pool.

vulnerability: Repeated switchToUnlocked corrupts accounting and can freeze the pool (DoS)
reason: switchToUnlocked only checks that the deposit timestamp is not greater than unlockedTimestampQualification. It does not check whether the deposit is already finished or already unlocked, and it unconditionally adds depositDetails.depositTokens to totalGymnetUnlocked on every call. An eligible attacker can call switchToUnlocked multiple times on the same deposit, or call it after withdrawing a finished deposit, inflating totalGymnetUnlocked without corresponding locked value. Both updatePool and pendingReward compute uint256 sharesTotal = totalGymnetLocked - totalGymnetUnlocked. Once totalGymnetUnlocked exceeds totalGymnetLocked, this subtraction underflows and reverts, causing updatePool and pendingReward to revert. This bricks deposits, withdrawals, claims, and reward accounting. Before the underflow, the inflated totalGymnetUnlocked also distorts reward-per-share calculations, allowing accounting manipulation and potentially unfair reward distribution or denial of service.

vulnerability: Unprotected initializer can be front-run for ownership takeover
reason: The initializer modifier only prevents multiple initializations; it does not restrict who may call the first initialization. If deployment and initialize are not executed atomically, an attacker can front-run the intended initialization and supply arbitrary _gym, _mlm, _pancakeRouterAddress, token arrays, reward rate, and start block. Because initialize calls __Ownable_init(), the attacker becomes owner, and runnerScriptAddress is also set to the attacker. As owner, the attacker can call privileged setters such as setTokenAddress, setPoolInfo, setIsPoolActive, setHolderRewardContractAddress, setVaultContractAddress, and setFarmingContractAddress to configure the pool maliciously. They can set arbitrary reward accounting via setPoolInfo, replace the staking token, activate the pool, and combine this with the fake-deposit and self-approval bug to drain deposited funds. This is a complete ownership takeover and can lead to theft of all tokens deposited by users.
